results.title: 6 Questions to Ask When Designing Teacher PD | TESOL | International Association
results.content: # 6 Questions to Ask When Designing Teacher PD. However, it is important to step back to consider other competencies that are equally important, but may receive insufficient attention in PD programming. Perhaps these other domains need the same time and effort as content-focused PD sessions. Where does this PD program fit within an overall, well-planned approach for school staff?**. Planning PD programs is similar, yet few of these factors are explicit in decision-making or design meetings. When will educators be able to apply the ideas presented in this PD program?**. Research suggests that successful PD design considers the necessary duration of the program, extends PD activities over the school year or semester, and “includes at least 20–40 hours of contact time.” Thinking beyond the content and skills focus or the logistics of the input sessions means considering financial resources; educator availability; the means to continue a structured, ongoing inquiry into the practices presented; and how sustained engagement will be supported and rewarded. Whose expertise is recognized in the design of this PD program?**. A recent survey of teachers in theUnited States found that “While teachers largely agree that school leaders think professional learning is important, just over half of teachers surveyed said they have ‘some say’ in their professional learning decisions, and nearly 20 percent said they have no input at all.” It is more important than ever that teachers play key roles in the design of PD at their institutions as the changing nature of today’s classroom makes teachers the most informed decision-makers. How is the learning in this PD program best measured?**. Yet teacher PD is often measured (if measured at all) only in regard to the engagement level or attendance of staff at meetings or sessions related to the program. In order to be truly thoughtful about the design of PD, we must consider the proficiency developed by educators as a result of the program and trace the results out to student learning outcomes. Why is this PD program important?**. However, it is all too often absent when delivering PD programming to educators. Take some time with your design team to consider these questions before you launch your next PD program!

results.title: Pupillary distance (PD): How to measure
results.content: # How to measure pupillary distance (PD). The pupillary distance (PD) measurement is a requirement for people who want to purchase eyeglasses. Here, find out how to measure your PD using a mirror and a ruler. Most children’s PD is 43–58 mm, and eye care professionals can measure this distance during an eye exam. Single or binocular PD measurement refers to the distance between the center of one pupil and the center of the other. ## How to measure PD using a ruler. A person can measure their PD by using a ruler. 4. The resulting measurement is the single PD. Individuals can also measure their single PD with the help of another person. To calculate a dual PD, people need to measure from one pupil to the bridge of the nose, note the measurement, and then do the same for the other eye. People should take several single and dual PD measurements and calculate the average distance to ensure a more accurate result. ## How to measure PD with glasses. This measurement is a person’s PD. Alternatively, a person can use their dual PD and subtract 1.5 mm from each eye’s measurement. An optician can measure PD when fitting glasses. However, a person who buys glasses online may need to measure their PD at home. Here, we answer some frequently asked questions about measuring PD. ### Is there an app to measure PD? People can also ask an eye care professional to measure their PD during an eye exam. ### Can you measure PD from old glasses? Yes, a person can measure their PD using their old glasses. ### What happens if my PD measurement is off? If a person does not have a correct PD measurement, it can affect the usefulness of glasses, especially progressive lenses. Someone who is unsure of their PD measurement may wish to contact an eye care professional to accurately measure the distance between their pupils. PD measures the space between a person’s pupils to ensure that their glasses and lenses fit correctly. Opticians will measure an individual’s PD when they are fitting glasses. Alternatively, a person can measure their PD at home.

results.title: What Works—and What Doesn't—in Teacher PD
results.content: Over the past two decades, professional development has focused on building teachers’ content knowledge, said Heather Hill, a principal investigator and professor at Harvard Graduate School of Education and a co-author of the paper. Instead, professional development that focused on changing teachers’ instructional practice—such as by identifying key teaching strategies and providing support for carrying out those changes in the classroom—was found to be more effective for improving student outcomes. The researchers hypothesized that content-focused professional development might not last long enough for teachers to learn enough about the subject to truly make a difference in their instruction. Also, those types of PD programs often don’t offer much support for the day-to-day practice, and teachers need to be able to connect their learning to their existing curriculum materials or lesson plans, the researchers said. The University of Virginia’s school of education offers professional-development support focused on improving teacher-student interactions. Still, teachers are tasked with helping students recover unfinished learning as a result of the pandemic, making effective professional development more important than ever, the researchers said.
